lf-dial.description: A control that sets how much of the page shows: Skim shows the lede, the gists and the headings above them, Read the page as written, and Everything also opens every closed detail.
lf-dial.instructions: Write it empty with a stable id, after the page's title and lede, on a page long enough that a reader might want only a quick pass. It governs the element it stands in and sticks within it, so write it directly in the element whose text it governs, such as the `layout-column` element, a sidebar page's body or a tab, not in a `header` holding the title. Skim is only as good as the gists: mark `.gist` the blocks that give a reader on a quick pass the page's argument and anything they must act on, reading coherently in order. A gist may be any block, and is often a picture, such as a figure, a chart, a video or a canvas. A section with nothing for that reader takes no gist, and folds whole (the detail package's author instructions).
lf-dial.example:
Why checkout latency doubled

A cache key change on Tuesday sent every checkout to the database.

Cause

The 4.2 release added the currency to the cart cache key, so no cached cart matched.

Hit rate fell from 94% to 3% within a minute of the deploy, and p99 rose from 180 ms to 410 ms.

The key, before and after 
cart:{user}  →  cart:{user}:{currency}

.gist.description: A block a reader on a quick pass needs, readable without the text around it: a passage's conclusion, or a picture, chart or video that shows the argument; with `lf-dial` at Skim, the lede, the gists and the headings above them are all that shows.
.gist.example:
Cause

The cache key changed, so no cached cart matched.

Hit rate fell from 94% to 3% within a minute of the deploy.
